title: Reverse Vowels of a String
spaceBreakdown:
- string s: modified in place; input/return value, not counted
- isVowel lambda: O(1) closure, no captures
- int left, right, char t: O(1) scalars
- recursion depth: none
approach: Use two pointers starting at opposite ends of the string. Advance each pointer inward until it lands on a vowel; when both do, swap them and continue. This reverses exactly the vowel subsequence while leaving every consonant in place, because each vowel is paired with its mirror-positioned vowel from the other end.
hints: If only the vowels move while every consonant stays put, which vowel from the original string must end up where the first vowel was? The string can be up to 3·10^5 characters.

Use two pointers, one at each end, each skipping non-vowels. In "IceCreAm", the left pointer stops on 'I' at index 0 and the right pointer stops on 'A' at index 6; swapping them yields "AceCreIm" so far.

```
left = 0, right = n - 1
while left < right:
    while left < right and s[left] is not a vowel: left += 1
    while left < right and s[right] is not a vowel: right -= 1
    if left < right:
        swap s[left] and s[right]
        left += 1
        right -= 1
return s
```

**Single character** - minimum input, no pair exists to swap.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: "a"`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `right = s.size()` (off-by-one) → reads s[n] out of bounds → returns garbage.

**No vowels** - every character is a consonant.
`Input: s = "bcdfg"` → `Expected: "bcdfg"`
⚠️ Bug: inner loop `while (!isVowel(s[left])) left++;` with no `left < right` guard → left runs past the end → out-of-bounds read → crash.

**All vowels** - every character is a vowel.
`Input: s = "aeiou"` → `Expected: "uoiea"`
⚠️ Bug: omitting `left++; right--;` after the swap → pointers never advance → infinite loop / TLE on "ae".

**Uppercase vowels** - mixed-case input.
`Input: s = "IceCreAm"` → `Expected: "AceCreIm"`
⚠️ Bug: checking only lowercase 'a','e','i','o','u' → treats 'I' and 'A' as consonants → returns "IceCreIm".

followUps.q: Reverse only the vowels within each word of a sentence (words separated by spaces), keeping word order.
followUps.a: Scan the string, identify word boundaries, and run the same two-pointer vowel reversal on each word's index range. TC O(n), SC O(1) extra (operate on the single buffer in place).

followUps.q: The set of "vowel" characters is now an arbitrary input parameter; how does that change the solution?
followUps.a: Build an unordered_set<char> from the parameter for O(1) membership tests, then run the identical two-pointer loop. TC O(n), SC O(k) where k is the vowel-set size.

followUps.q: The string arrives as a stream too large to hold in memory; produce the reversed-vowel stream.
followUps.a: First pass: stream once, pushing each vowel onto a stack. Second pass: stream again, emitting each character unchanged unless it is a vowel, in which case pop the stack. TC O(n), SC O(v) where v is the number of vowels.
